papers.title: Quantitative FS-domains over continuous t-norms
papers.abstract: We introduce quantitative FS-domains over continuous t-norms using a scalar-valued finite-separation degree and an approximate identity. The construction recovers classical FS-domains over the Boolean base. Symmetric quantitative FS-domains are characterized by compactness of their ball topology. In particular, a complete metric space is a quantitative FS-domain if and only if it is compact. Quantitative FS-domains are continuous and form a symmetric monoidal closed category under tensor products and function spaces of Yoneda-continuous maps. This category is Cartesian closed exactly for the G\"odel t-norm.

papers.title: Polynomiality ideals, with applications to polynomial functors over free nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a unital commutative ring. For a monoidal category $C$ whose unit is a zero object, we introduce a descending filtration of the k-linearization of $C$ by two-sided ideals, called the polynomiality ideals: the $d$-th ideal encodes polynomiality of degree at most $d$ for functors from $C$ to $k$-modules. These ideals yield general criteria for the existence of polynomial functors of a given degree and for equivalences between the categories of polynomial functors of degree at most $d$ over different base categories. For Lawvere theories satisfying a mild condition, we identify the polynomiality ideals with powers of augmentation ideals of monoids; this identification makes the criteria computable by means of classical group ring theory. As the main application, we study polynomial functors over finitely generated free nilpotent groups, comparing them across nilpotency classes and polynomial degrees. We obtain refinements of results of Baues and Pirashvili in the case of class at most 2, recover several folklore results for free groups and free abelian groups, and establish a modular analogue formulated with dimension subgroups over a field of positive characteristic in place of the lower central series. Finally, we show that, in contrast to polynomial functors, analytic functors admit no analogous ideal in most cases.

papers.title: Maximality of the Do\v{s}en-Petri\'{c} Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Every congruence preserved by the operations on morphisms and by uniform formula substitution either is equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. We give two proofs that use Boolean Coherence and uniform formula substitution to derive equality of the product projections from an identification of distinct parallel morphisms. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.
